companion_sources.locator: The Merchant of Venice IV.1, Portia's mercy speech; not the whole trial outcome; snapshot lines 79556–79578
companion_sources.text:
PORTIA. The quality of mercy is not strain'd;
    It droppeth as the gentle rain from heaven
    Upon the place beneath. It is twice blest:
    It blesseth him that gives and him that takes.
    'Tis mightiest in the mightiest; it becomes
    The throned monarch better than his crown;
    His sceptre shows the force of temporal power,
    The attribute to awe and majesty,
    Wherein doth sit the dread and fear of kings;
    But mercy is above this sceptred sway,
    It is enthroned in the hearts of kings,
    It is an attribute to God himself;
    And earthly power doth then show likest God's
    When mercy seasons justice. Therefore, Jew,
    Though justice be thy plea, consider this-
    That in the course of justice none of us
    Should see salvation; we do pray for mercy,
    And that same prayer doth teach us all to render
    The deeds of mercy. I have spoke thus much
    To mitigate the justice of thy plea,
    Which if thou follow, this strict court of Venice
    Must needs give sentence 'gainst the merchant there.
companion_sources.title: Portia's appeal

Shared chronology does not prove collaboration with Shakespeare. No score, lyrics or recording are supplied.

source_es.text:
Solo contexto y guía de lectura o escucha; sin grabaciones ni partituras modernas protegidas. El contexto religioso se describe, no se evalúa como devoción.

Identifiquen Flow My Tears de Dowland en el Second Booke of Songs de 1600. Comparen una canción impresa con una canción dentro de una obra teatral. Una escucha real requiere una fuente legítima aportada por el adulto.

Si hay fuentes legítimas disponibles, comparen una pieza de teclado de Byrd, como The Earl of Salisbury's Pavan, con la canción de Dowland. No atribuyan a Byrd la canción de Shakespeare.

Construyan una cronología de las publicaciones citadas y de una obra de Shakespeare revisada. Ser contemporáneos no prueba colaboración ni que una grabación reproduzca el estreno.

Referencias bibliográficas: John Dowland, Flow My Tears, The Second Book of Songes, n.º 2 (1600), canción para voz y laúd: https://imslp.org/wiki/Flow_My_Tears_(Dowland,_John)
William Byrd, The Earl of Salisbury Pavan, pieza para teclado publicada en Parthenia (1613): https://imslp.org/wiki/The_Earl_of_Salisbury_Pavan_and_2_Galliards_(Byrd,_William)
La coincidencia de época no demuestra colaboración con Shakespeare. No se aporta ninguna partitura, letra ni grabación.

Context and score/listening guidance only; no copyrighted recording or modern score is supplied. Religious context is descriptive, not devotional assessment.

Identify Dowland's Flow My Tears in the Second Booke of Songs (1600). Compare the role of a printed song with a song spoken in a Shakespeare play. Use a lawful source if actual listening or score analysis is attempted.

Use an adult-provided lawful example of Byrd's keyboard music, such as The Earl of Salisbury's Pavan. Compare its phrase organization with the adult-selected Dowland source. Do not claim Byrd wrote the Shakespeare song.

Build a dated timeline of the cited publications and a reviewed Shakespeare play. Contemporary lives are not proof that these artists collaborated or that a particular recording is authentic to a first performance.

Bibliographic references: John Dowland, Flow My Tears, The Second Book of Songes, no. 2 (1600), song for voice and lute: https://imslp.org/wiki/Flow_My_Tears_(Dowland,_John)
William Byrd, The Earl of Salisbury Pavan, keyboard piece published in Parthenia (1613): https://imslp.org/wiki/The_Earl_of_Salisbury_Pavan_and_2_Galliards_(Byrd,_William)
Shared chronology does not prove collaboration with Shakespeare. No score, lyrics or recording are supplied.

source_es.text:
Solo contexto y guía de lectura o escucha; sin grabaciones ni partituras modernas protegidas. El contexto religioso se describe, no se evalúa como devoción.

Identifiquen Flow My Tears de Dowland en el Second Booke of Songs de 1600. Comparen una canción impresa con una canción dentro de una obra teatral. Una escucha real requiere una fuente legítima aportada por el adulto.

Si hay fuentes legítimas disponibles, comparen una pieza de teclado de Byrd, como The Earl of Salisbury's Pavan, con la canción de Dowland. No atribuyan a Byrd la canción de Shakespeare.

Construyan una cronología de las publicaciones citadas y de una obra de Shakespeare revisada. Ser contemporáneos no prueba colaboración ni que una grabación reproduzca el estreno.

Referencias bibliográficas: John Dowland, Flow My Tears, The Second Book of Songes, n.º 2 (1600), canción para voz y laúd: https://imslp.org/wiki/Flow_My_Tears_(Dowland,_John)
William Byrd, The Earl of Salisbury Pavan, pieza para teclado publicada en Parthenia (1613): https://imslp.org/wiki/The_Earl_of_Salisbury_Pavan_and_2_Galliards_(Byrd,_William)
La coincidencia de época no demuestra colaboración con Shakespeare. No se aporta ninguna partitura, letra ni grabación.
